mappings.note: Defines continent, ocean and island - the vocabulary needed before continents and oceans can be located on the world map. Not LO-2, because nothing about life or the earth's spheres is asked.
Draw the continents freehand and check them against the map; this is the recall-and-locate half of LO-5. Not LO-8, since no scale, symbols or neighbourhood map are involved.
Label every continent and ocean on an outline world map - the literal wording of LO-5. Not LO-6, no latitude or longitude is read.
Crossword clue for 'island', a landmass short of a continent surrounded by sea; it tests the continent/island/ocean distinction of LO-5. Not LO-7, because no Indian island is named.
The blue planet's colour comes from its water cover, which is the hydrosphere among the earth's zones in LO-2. Not LO-5, since no ocean is named or located.
Identifies oceans as the largest water bodies - naming the ocean category that LO-5 asks pupils to place on the world map.
Identifies a continent as a large continuous landmass; the land counterpart of the ocean-definition item and under the same outcome.

Asks what oceans and continents DO for the planet - shaping climate and so the conditions for life, which is the habitability sense of LO-2. Not LO-5, which is about locating them, not their planetary role.

The Indian Navy's motto invoking the Vedic deity Varuna is a cultural-tradition item, so it belongs under C-SST4.2 rather than any geography outcome. Held at competency level because LO-25 asks for ANALYSIS of ancient ideas and this is recall of a motto.
Salinity as the reason seawater cannot be drunk by land animals - a property of the hydrosphere bearing directly on life. Not LO-5: no ocean is being located.

Water scarcity despite abundant water, because nearly all of it is saline; this is the fresh-water share of the earth's water zones. Distinct from the salinity item in asking about the consequence, but the frame offers the same outcome.
How many oceans are conventionally recognised - the count a pupil must know before labelling them on a world map.
The Pacific as the largest ocean; a relative-size fact about the named oceans of LO-5, not about the earth's spheres.
Identifies the Indian Ocean from the continents that enclose it - a genuinely map-based item pairing oceans with continents, which is LO-5's core.
The Arctic as the smallest ocean; the mirror of the Pacific item and under the same outcome, since LO-5 is the only one naming oceans.
Defines flora, which is plant life - the biosphere that LO-2 singles out. Not LO-5, since no place is located.
Places the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal within the Indian Ocean - locating water bodies relative to an ocean on the world map. Not LO-7, because the seas are not India's own physical features.

Requires locating Lakshadweep in the Arabian Sea on the map of India, so LO-7 for the Indian feature and LO-5 for the water body it sits in. Not LO-6: the item asks for position relative to a sea, not a coordinate.
Why the continent count runs from four to seven - a point about how the continents of LO-5 are conventionally divided rather than about the earth as a habitat.
The Olympic rings as the five inhabited continents; a recall item about which continents are counted, so LO-5.
Compares North and South America by area from the chapter diagram - reading relative continent size off a map, which is LO-5.
Defines an island as land surrounded by water on all sides; the same land-and-water vocabulary as the crossword clue, and again LO-5 rather than the earth's zones.
Greenland as the world's largest island - a locate-and-name item on the world map. Not LO-7, because Greenland is not an Indian feature.

Names India's second island group, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; an Indian feature to be placed on the map of India (LO-7), in the Bay of Bengal (LO-5). Paired with the Lakshadweep item for the same reason.

Asks the NAME of India's first Antarctic base, i.e. India's contribution in science, which LO-24 covers ('such as' is illustrative, not exhaustive). Deliberately not LO-5, which is used for the sibling item that asks which CONTINENT the station stands on.
World Oceans Day exists to press the ocean's role in sustaining life, which is the habitability theme of LO-2. Not LO-5: no ocean is named or located.
Three-fourths of the surface under water - the extent of the hydrosphere among the earth's zones. Grouped with the blue-planet items, which the frame gives no finer outcome for.

The distractor that decides the item is 'Indian Ocean entirely in the Southern Hemisphere', so the pupil must know both the ocean's place (LO-5) and where the Equator cuts it (LO-6). The other options are pure size facts.
Seas, bays and gulfs as partly enclosed arms of oceans - subdivisions of the ocean vocabulary of LO-5, not a property of the hydrosphere.
Answer is the CONTINENT Antarctica, so this is continent identification. Kept apart from the Dakshin Gangotri naming item, which was mapped to India's scientific contribution instead.

Land and water are unevenly spread over the globe - a statement about the world-map distribution of continents and oceans. Not LO-2, which would be right only if the point were about life or the spheres.
Assertion-reason on ocean boundaries being conventional rather than natural; a point about how the oceans of LO-5 are delimited on a map.
Matches a sea or gulf to its parent ocean, which is world-map placement. Not LO-7 even though the Arabian Sea borders India, because the question is about the ocean it belongs to.
Why astronauts called the earth the blue planet - the ocean cover seen from space, again the hydrosphere of LO-2 rather than any locating task.
Fresh water versus seawater by salinity; a property of the earth's water that decides what is drinkable and so habitable. Not LO-5, no ocean is placed.
Groundwater as water stored below the surface - another component of the earth's water zones. Distinct in content from the seawater items but the frame offers only this one outcome.
Marine species spread across oceans because the water circulates: an explicitly biosphere claim, which is what LO-2 names. Not LO-5, since no ocean has to be located.
